claims.text: Large Language Models produce hallucinations, generating plausible-sounding but factually incorrect responses.
Knowledge Graphs represent structured collections of interconnected facts as entities and relationships.

evidence.description: LLMs face a significant challenge of hallucinations, where models produce plausible-sounding but factually incorrect responses.
Knowledge Graphs (KGs) provide a structured collection of interconnected facts represented as entities (nodes) and their relationships (edges).

limitations.text: Hallucinations in Large Language Models undermine trust and limit their applicability across different domains.

future_work.text: Addressing unresolved open problems in knowledge integration methods for LLM systems.
Developing advanced frameworks and benchmarks for evaluating hallucinations in KG-supported LLM systems.
